raw_response: {"diagnosis": "raw_transactions has 4972 rows but only 4827 distinct txn_id values, so some transactions were delivered more than once (likely re-sent across batches), and silver_transactions passes the duplicate POSTED rows straight through. The fix keeps one POSTED row per txn_id, choosing the most recently ingested copy; the duplicate rows themselves were not sampled, so this assumes they are re-deliveries rather than distinct transactions sharing an id.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.6, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts DESC, batch_id DESC) = 1"}}
